method: first-match-wins over commodities.json in array order through grocery/match-lib.ps1 New-CommodityMatcher + Resolve-Commodity (the same compiled oracle compare-deals uses, 592 commodities, 85 global excludes), with per-unit estimated by pricing-math-lib.ps1 Get-UnitPrice on the part name + part size against the routed commodity object. BEFORE = the whole ad line routed as one name with the file row size; AFTER = each split part routed on its own with its own size. Only names the split rule touches can change; every other name in the corpus is unaffected by construction.

corpus.description: newest out\regular\*-regular-*.json per store prefix (hunter-* included) + newest out\ads-*.json + newest bakers/fareway deals file + sams-deals-2026-09-11 (the live Baker ad week is 2026-09-09..09-15). Every section reads this one list.

split_rule.text: split a weekly-ad line on " or " only when EVERY resulting segment ends in its own size expression (number + fl oz/oz/ct/lb/pk/pack/rolls/ml/l/gal/qt/pt/count/ea, optionally followed by one packaging noun bag/bottle(s)/can(s)/jar/box/pkg/package/carton), after stripping a trailing ", In the Bakery" / ", Select Varieties"; a segment with no size is a variety alternation and is glued to the following segment; a line where any segment fails is left WHOLE
split_rule.loose_rule_rejected: a looser rule (any segment carrying a size anywhere) also fired on 39 Hy-Vee ads lines of the shape "A size, B size, $price", produced parts like "cans 12 fl. oz., $9.99", and would have created a WRONG-PRODUCT coffee crown from "ice coffee 50.7 oz., 3/ $10.00" (coffee | Hy-Vee 0.3857 -> 0.0657, crown Aldi 0.3825 taken). Measured, then rejected; see loose_rule_effects.
